clue.text: My French wine, cold according to order?

parts.note: mon is French for my
Asti is an Italian sparkling wine
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: Someone describes a French wine served chilled exactly as the instructions say.
explanation.walkthrough: 'according to order' looks like 'as instructed', but the order is a religious order of monks.
explanation.definitionFit: Monastic life follows the rule of a religious order, so monastic means living by such a rule.

clue.text: Birds in the morning rising with bird noises

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means read upwards, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: a.m. stands for the morning
caws are the cries of crows

explanation.surface: Birds getting up at dawn amid the croaking of crows.
explanation.definitionFit: Macaws are large brightly coloured parrots, so they are birds.

clue.text: Geordie Socialist, say, embracing one nymph

parts.note: a Geordie is from Tyneside in the north-east of England, NE

indicators.note: embracing means hugging, so the socialist word holds the other

parts.note: red is a common term for a socialist
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A left-wing Newcastle man hugs a mythical nymph.
explanation.walkthrough: A Geordie is a native of Newcastle in north-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: The Nereids were sea nymphs in Greek mythology, daughters of Nereus.

clue.text: False son cherished — father ultimately coming out

indicators.note: coming out means leaving, so that letter is removed

parts.note: precious means dearly loved, cherished

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the word father

explanation.surface: A son wrongly treasured as his dad finally comes out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming out' removes R, the last letter of father, from PRECIOUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Specious means superficially plausible but actually wrong, hence false.

clue.text: French island has unknown shrub with prickles

parts.note: île is French for island
x is an unknown quantity in algebra

explanation.surface: An island off France has a mystery prickly bush.
explanation.definitionFit: Ilex is the holly genus, a shrub with spiny leaves.

clue.text: Recorded as being cut down and processed?

definitions.meaning: to log something is to record it, as in a ship's log
trees that are ... are felled and cut up for timber

explanation.surface: Something noted down as having been felled and handled.
explanation.definitionFit: Logging is both entering details in a record and felling trees and cutting them into lengths.

clue.text: Obscure work — a search with street cleared

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work

indicators.note: cleared means taken away, so the street letters are removed

parts.note: a quest is a search

explanation.surface: A dull task: hunting for something once the road has been emptied.
explanation.definitionFit: Opaque means not transparent and hence hard to understand, obscure.

clue.text: Having a spat? Agreed to differ about the thing looked for

indicators.note: about means around, so the rearranged letters surround the other piece
letters made to differ from their order are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
in hide-and-seek and tag, 'it' is the one being sought

explanation.surface: People quarrelling agree to disagree over something they were hunting for.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spat' looks like a quarrel; it is a short gaiter covering the ankle, a sense more common in British usage.
explanation.definitionFit: A spat is a cloth ankle covering, a kind of gaiter, so wearing one is being gaitered.

clue.text: Spooner's card game ruined, proving to be a trial

indicators.note: Spooner's tells us the opening sounds of the two words are swapped

parts.note: rummy is a card game
done in the sense of done for, ruined

explanation.surface: A card game spoiled, as someone's experiment turns out.
explanation.walkthrough: Swapping the opening R and D sounds of RUMMY DONE gives DUMMY RUN, with 'done' pronounced 'dun'.
explanation.definitionFit: A dummy run is a practice or rehearsal, a trial before the real thing.

clue.text: Rushed, being worried — always getting blocked in

indicators.note: a word that gets blocked in is penned inside another, so it sits within the other word

parts.note: to have cared is to have been worried or concerned
e'er is a poetic contraction of ever, meaning always

explanation.surface: Someone dashed about anxiously, forever stuck in traffic.
explanation.definitionFit: To career is to move swiftly and wildly, so careered is a synonym of rushed.

clue.text: Conservative is entertained by group of stars showing prejudice

indicators.note: a guest entertained by a host is taken in, so these letters go inside the others

parts.note: the Ram is the constellation Aries

explanation.surface: A Tory politician is hosted by a celebrity group and shows bigotry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'group of stars' suggests celebrities; here it is the constellation the Ram.
explanation.definitionFit: Racism is prejudice against people because of their race, a specific kind of prejudice.

clue.text: Guarding hard border

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils
edging is a border or trim

explanation.surface: A tough frontier is kept protected.
explanation.definitionFit: Hedging means protecting oneself against loss, as in hedging a bet, so guarding.

clue.text: Gather for voting — with it gaining external victory

indicators.note: the trendy word gains something on its outside, so the victory word wraps round it

parts.note: a win is a victory
hip means fashionable, with it

explanation.surface: A party rounds up supporters for a vote, being trendy and securing a win from outside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with it' reads like a link phrase, but it is slang for fashionable.
explanation.definitionFit: In Parliament a whip calls in members to vote, so to whip in is to round them up for a division.

clue.text: Dessert left out May's neighbour's tucked into in naive fashion

indicators.note: something tucked into another is placed snugly inside it
out tells us the left letter is dropped from the dessert

parts.note: jelly is a wobbly dessert
June comes next to May in the calendar; the 's is read as is

explanation.surface: A pudding without its leftovers, and a neighbour called May tucks in naively.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' removes one L from JELLY, leaving JELY, which then holds JUNE.
explanation.definitionFit: Jejune means simplistic or naive, so jejunely describes acting in a naive, unsophisticated way.

clue.text: Fabric in room is about to be put on ceiling

indicators.note: in a down clue the ceiling is the top, so this letter goes first

parts.note: C is short for circa, about
a hall is a room

explanation.surface: Fabric in a room is going to be fixed to the ceiling.
explanation.definitionFit: Challis is a soft lightweight woven fabric of wool or cotton.

clue.text: In the manner in which greedy types will get clams to eat

parts.note: qua is Latin used in English for 'in the capacity of, as'
hogs are greedy people who take more than their share

explanation.surface: Greedy people are expected to wolf down clams.
explanation.definitionFit: The quahog is an edible hard-shelled clam from the North American Atlantic coast.

clue.text: List of players joining United

parts.note: men are the players in a team or game, such as chessmen
U is the abbreviation for United, as in football club names

explanation.surface: A team sheet of players signing for a United football club.
explanation.definitionFit: A menu is a list, of dishes or of options on a screen.

clue.text: Mountain climbing on rope that can be eased

indicators.note: in a down clue climbing means going up, so the word reads backwards

parts.note: an alp is a mountain
a cable is a thick rope

explanation.surface: Climbing a peak on a rope that can be loosened.
explanation.definitionFit: Placable means able to be appeased or soothed, so something that can be eased.

clue.text: Arachnid ruined crop in heavenly place

indicators.note: in says the scrambled letters sit inside the place name

parts.note: Sion, or Zion, is the heavenly city

indicators.note: ruined letters are wrecked and reassembled

explanation.surface: A spider-like creature spoiled crops in paradise.
explanation.definitionFit: A scorpion is an arachnid, in the same class as spiders.

clue.text: Any power may come from guns etc

indicators.note: may come from says a new word can be made out of these letters

explanation.surface: Any force may derive from firearms.
explanation.definitionFit: Weaponry is weapons collectively, guns being one example.

clue.text: Philosopher said 'Shut up!'

indicators.note: said tells us the name is taken as it is pronounced, not as written

parts.note: John Locke was an English philosopher

explanation.surface: A philosopher snapped at someone to be quiet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shut up!' looks like 'be quiet'; read it as an order to secure something.
explanation.definitionFit: To lock something is to shut it up securely, as in locking up a house.

clue.text: Servant chucked, no good with security device

indicators.note: no means without, so the good letter is removed

parts.note: flung means thrown, chucked
a key secures a lock

explanation.surface: A servant gets sacked, being useless, along with the house keys.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chucked' suggests a sacking but it is a synonym for thrown.
explanation.definitionFit: A flunkey is a liveried manservant or footman, a type of servant.

clue.text: Buddhist school has an area providing female accommodation

parts.note: Zen is a school of Mahayana Buddhism

explanation.surface: A Buddhist school has a zone set aside for women.
explanation.definitionFit: A zenana is the women's quarters in a household in India and Iran.

clue.text: Cite a Fascist leader stammering

parts.note: Il Duce was Mussolini's title as Fascist leader of Italy; stammering repeats his opening letter, D-Duce

explanation.surface: Quote a Fascist dictator who stutters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stammering' doubles the D of DUCE, as a stutterer would say D-Duce.
explanation.definitionFit: To adduce is to cite or put forward as evidence.

clue.text: Nothing wrong with the last thing that is used for a soup?

definitions.text: thing that is used for a soup?

parts.note: O is the round symbol for nothing, zero
X is the cross marking an answer wrong
the tail is the last part, the end

explanation.surface: Nothing wrong with the final item served for soup.
explanation.definitionFit: The tail of an ox is a classic soup ingredient, giving oxtail soup.

clue.text: Philanthropist seen heading off fiddling with cigar

indicators.note: fiddling with letters plays them about into a new order
heading off says the first letter of the word is cut away

explanation.surface: A wealthy benefactor is spotted toying with a cigar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading off' drops S from 'seen' to leave EEN, which is mixed up with CIGAR by 'fiddling with'.
explanation.definitionFit: Andrew Carnegie, the steel magnate, gave away most of his fortune, a famous philanthropist.

clue.text: Cluster of flowers in spring, ten in Versailles

parts.note: a spa is a mineral spring
dix is French for ten, Versailles standing for France

explanation.surface: Flowers blooming in spring, ten of them at the French palace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spring' looks like the season; here it is a water source.
explanation.definitionFit: A spadix is a fleshy spike of tiny flowers, as in arum lilies, so a flower cluster.

clue.text: Friend's call making further play impossible

definitions.meaning: a friend; the 's reads as is
in chess, ... (checkmate) is announced when the king cannot escape and the game ends

explanation.surface: A friend's announcement ends the game for good.
explanation.definitionFit: Mate is a pal, and also checkmate, which finishes a chess game.

clue.text: March at the match may be this — control, we hear, is needed

definitions.text: March at the match may be this

indicators.note: we hear says the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: to bridle is to restrain or control

explanation.surface: At a sports match, marchers need to be kept under control.
explanation.walkthrough: 'match' means a marriage, not a sporting fixture, and the march is a wedding march.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bridal March from Wagner's Lohengrin is played at weddings, a match being a marriage.

clue.text: Wax from a can manipulated with a rub

indicators.note: manipulated means handled and worked, so these letters are reworked

explanation.surface: Polish obtained from a tin and worked in with a rub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'manipulated' rearranges CAN plus A RUB into CARNAUB; the first A of the clue completes the word.
explanation.definitionFit: Carnauba is a hard wax from the leaves of a Brazilian palm, used in polishes.

clue.text: Any promotion reported to be needed for group of nine?

indicators.note: reported tells us the words are given by how they are spoken

parts.note: any is said, then ad, a promotion or advertisement

explanation.surface: Any advertising, it is said, will be required for a nine-strong group.
explanation.definitionFit: An ennead is a set of nine, from the Greek for nine.

clue.text: Extremely useful source of water, all right?

parts.note: very means extremely
a well is a source of water

explanation.surface: A very good water supply, someone asks if that is acceptable.
explanation.definitionFit: 'Very well' is said to agree to something, just like 'all right'.
